clue.text: A month in lodge, a sure-fire winner

indicators.note: 'in' places the first words inside the word that follows, as something lodged within

blocks.note: taken as written
FEB is the short form of February
to lodge something is to set it firmly in place

explanation.surface: A horse lodged at a stable for a month is tipped as the certain winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodge' looks like a noun for a cabin or a beaver's home; here it is the verb meaning to fix or place.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe bet is a wager or choice almost certain to succeed, so a sure-fire winner.

clue.text: Scallywag, one getting large prawns

blocks.note: a scamp is a mischievous rascal
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rascal makes off with a plate of big prawns.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are Dublin Bay prawns or langoustines, larger than ordinary shrimps, often served breaded.

clue.text: Charge exorbitantly for wool

blocks.note: first meaning: to swindle someone by overcharging
second meaning: the woolly coat shorn from a sheep

explanation.surface: A trader asks a ridiculous price for some wool.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece is slang for robbing by overpricing, and a fleece is the shorn coat of a sheep.

clue.text: Bird coming from shift on Rhode Island paper's upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word for paper reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: to budge is to shift slightly
RI is the US state abbreviation
a rag is a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A bird appears after a shift on Rhode Island has upset the local paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The budgerigar is a small Australian parakeet, a popular cage bird.

clue.text: Unexpectedly alters fortnight for tug of war

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly breaks the expected order, so the letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Plans for a tug of war are suddenly moved by two weeks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug of war, two teams pulling on a rope, is a classic contest of brute power, and the phrase is used figuratively too.

clue.text: Metal grille in neat pub

blocks.note: neat is an old word for cattle, and a bull is one
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A tidy pub has a metal grille in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like 'tidy' but is the archaic noun for oxen or cattle, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull bar is a metal frame fitted to the front of a vehicle to protect it in collisions with animals.

clue.text: Responsible for the emotional outbursts out of public view

blocks.note: to be behind something is to be responsible for it
taken as written
making a scene means an emotional outburst in public

explanation.surface: Someone is blamed for the tantrums that happened in private.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind the scenes is an idiom, from the theatre backstage, for happening in secret or away from the audience.

clue.text: Left on vessel for a carefree adventure

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
an ark is a vessel, like Noah's; in a down clue the first letter sits on it

explanation.surface: Someone sets off aboard a boat for a light-hearted escapade.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of fun or a mischievous escapade done for amusement.

clue.text: Made tame remark, initially, getting permission to enter African country

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it
to enter a country is to go inside it, so these letters go within the country's name

blocks.note: the first letter of remark
an OK is a go-ahead
Benin is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed into an African country after a remark that they had domesticated something.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted letters go in after the country's first letter, not in its exact middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that is broken in has been trained to accept a rider, which is to say tamed.

clue.text: Hen's dark — unusual bird

indicators.note: unusual suggests these letters are out of their usual order and need rearranging

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hen has unusually dark plumage for its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The redshank is a wading bird named for its bright orange-red legs.

clue.text: Change the last word, last in ballad

indicators.note: last in tells us to keep only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer
the closing letter of ballad

explanation.surface: A songwriter alters the final word at the end of a ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text is to change or correct it.

clue.text: Novelist in forest, following one

indicators.note: following means the forest word is placed after the word for one

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
Sherwood Forest in Nottinghamshire, home of Robin Hood

explanation.surface: A writer is found in the woods, trailing behind someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was an English novelist, author of Goodbye to Berlin.

clue.text: Some in labour dispute choose bar round the centre of Exeter

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, here the middle pair of a six-letter place name
round means the preceding words wrap around what follows

blocks.note: to pick is to choose
the two central letters of Exeter
a bar is a stripe or line

explanation.surface: Workers in an industrial dispute pick a pub near the middle of Exeter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' wants to be a pub in this surface; it is a stripe. Exeter has six letters, so its centre is the middle pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A picket line is the group of striking workers standing outside a workplace, so some of those in a labour dispute.

clue.text: Net used in game show

indicators.note: used in signals the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: runs across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A net is a prop in a television game show.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesh is netted material, a fabric of interlaced threads with gaps.

clue.text: Chaotic times at one dwelling place

indicators.note: chaotic means in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Life gets hectic at a single home now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a flat on two floors with its own entrance, a type of home.

clue.text: Besottedness shown by a fan out in it, excited

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are thrown about into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An admirer, worked up and out of control, shows a passionate crush.
explanation.definitionFit: Infatuation is an intense, foolish passion, the state of being besotted.

clue.text: A strong drink bites, as one who's had too much might say?

indicators.text: as one who's had too much might say
indicators.note: this points to a drunkard's slurred pronunciation, so a word is heard as a tipsy speaker would voice it

blocks.note: bites is snaps, slurred with a drunken sh

explanation.surface: A potent spirit has a real bite, slurs a tipsy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Snaps means bites; said by someone drunk it comes out 'shnaps'. The question mark flags the playful sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong clear spirit, typically German and distilled from fruit or grain.

clue.text: Unstable dyes aunt mixed

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters are combined in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An aunt mixes some dyes that do not hold their colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsteady and unstable are synonyms, both meaning liable to wobble or fall.

clue.text: Get in touch with the French about new visual aid

indicators.note: about means going around, so the French article surrounds the letter for new

blocks.note: to contact someone is to get in touch
les is French for the (plural)
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Contact the French about a new aid for eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' must be the plural article, since the singular le or la cannot give the needed S.
explanation.definitionFit: A contact lens sits on the eye to correct sight, so it helps one see.

clue.text: Hunter quick-thinking? Not half with gun

indicators.note: not half tells us to drop half of the previous word, keeping only its front portion

blocks.note: nimble describes a quick, agile mind
rod is old American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: A hunter is half as quick-witted as needed with a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimrod is the mighty hunter of Genesis, and his name is used for any keen huntsman.

clue.text: French artist in US city, one on river

blocks.note: Reno is a city in Nevada
the Roman numeral for one
R abbreviates river; in a down clue the previous letter sits on it

explanation.surface: A French painter is in an American city, one beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a leading French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Short informal letter college rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the college name is read backwards

blocks.note: Eton is the famous English public school, Eton College

explanation.surface: A college sends a brief letter turning an applicant down.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is a brief informal written message.

clue.text: Clarinet playing in extremely memorable commercial

indicators.note: an instrument playing is being worked, so its letters are moved around
extremely points to the very ends of the next word, its first and last letters
in places the jumbled letters inside the outer letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of memorable
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A clarinet plays in an especially memorable advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial' looks like a noun meaning advert, but the answer is the adjective about trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile means concerned with trade and merchants, which is what commercial means as an adjective.

clue.text: One politician, one with group of warriors

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single politician goes about with a band of fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment or armed band, a crossword-friendly word for a body of soldiers.

clue.text: On first of pages, a migrant dicky bird

indicators.note: first of means take only the opening letter of the next word
dicky is British slang for faulty or shaky, so these letters are in poor order

blocks.note: the first letter of pages
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wandering bird with a dodgy heart features in the pages of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky bird' reads as childish for any bird; dicky (British for unsound, as in a dicky heart) is the jumble signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse of mountains and the Arctic that turns white in winter.

clue.text: Trunk and spreading roots

indicators.note: spreading suggests things fanning out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree is described as having a trunk with roots fanning out.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree picture makes 'Trunk' a tree part, but it is the trunk of the human body.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the body, everything but head and limbs.

clue.text: Elegant pen is held in left hand

indicators.note: held in means gripped within, so the short word goes inside the two hand-related letters

blocks.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
taken as written
L and H abbreviate left and hand

explanation.surface: A smart fountain pen is held in someone's left hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' reads as a writing tool; it is the animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish means fashionable and smart, which is to say elegant.

clue.text: Narrow lake shown in poster

indicators.note: shown in means displayed inside, so the single letter goes within the other word

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for lake
a poster is someone who posts something, a sender

explanation.surface: A slim lake features in an advertising poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poster' suggests a placard, but it is read as one who posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means thin or narrow in width.
